message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's morally acceptable for me to tell my cousin that his kid can't stay in our house. Let me break this down step by step. First, my cousin moved in with my husband and me. We converted the main bedroom and bathroom into a separate flatlet for him, so he has his own entrance and it's like two separate units in one house. That seems pretty accommodating on our part. Now, my cousin has a 2-year-old, and he's going through a custody battle with his ex. He wants to spend more time with his son, and I completely support that. I really hope he gets more time with his son. Yesterday, he asked if we could convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son, so when he comes over weekends, his son can stay there. But here's the thing: there's no access from my cousin's room into our part of the house, and he doesn't have keys to come and go as he pleases. So, if his son is staying in our house, he can't get to his son easily, and I'm not comfortable with that. I understand that the court is looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son. His current room and bathroom are more than big enough, so I don't think the court would have any issues with that. But I'm not willing to take responsibility for his kid. I don't feel comfortable having his son in our house without him having easy access. The whole family is involved in this because that's just how my family is. Everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his current custody situation to get him more time with his son. But I'm not sure if I should go along with this. So, the question is: Would it be wrong (WIBTA) for me to tell my cousin I won't allow his son to stay in our house and potentially jeopardize his court case? Let me think about the moral aspects here. On one hand, I'm supporting my cousin by letting him live with us and helping him with his custody battle. On the other hand, I'm not comfortable with his son staying in our house without him having easy access, and I don't want to take responsibility for his kid. Is it morally acceptable for me to prioritize my own comfort and boundaries over my cousin's custody case? Or should I set aside my discomfort to help him get more time with his son? I guess I need to consider the potential consequences. If I say no, it might affect his custody case, which could mean he spends less time with his son. But if I say yes, I'm putting myself in a situation I'm not comfortable with. Maybe there's a middle ground. Could we find another arrangement that makes everyone comfortable? Or is it better to be honest about my boundaries and let him find another solution? I'm also thinking about the family dynamics. Everyone expects me to help, but I have my own limits. It's important to respect my own boundaries while still being supportive. In the end, I have to decide whether my discomfort justifies potentially harming my cousin's custody case. It's a tough call, but I think it's more important to be honest about my limits rather than compromise my own well-being.
